hints: Notice the given data $l = (87.3 \pm 0.2) \text{ cm}$ and $T = (1.9 \pm 0.05) \text{ s}$ and first work out $0.2/87.3$ and $0.05/1.9$ as percentage uncertainties.
Rearrange $T = 2\pi\sqrt{l/g}$ to $g = 4\pi^2 l/T^2$ so $g$ is proportional to $l$ to power $1$ and to $T$ to power $-2$.

Recall that for multiplication and division percentage uncertainties add, and a squared quantity contributes twice its percentage uncertainty - so combine one times the $l$ term with two times the $T$ term.
walkthrough: Write the equation with $g$ as subject: $T = 2\pi\sqrt{l/g}$ gives $T^2 = 4\pi^2 l/g$, so $g = 4\pi^2 l/T^2$. The constant $4\pi^2$ has no uncertainty.
Calculate the percentage uncertainty in $T$: $(0.05/1.9) \times 100\% \approx 2.63\%$. Since $g \propto 1/T^2$, the $T$ contribution is doubled: $2 \times 2.63\% \approx 5.26\%$.
Add contributions for the $l/T^2$ combination: $0.23\% + 5.26\% \approx 5.49\%$, about $5.5\%$ with sensible precision.
